newsitem.title: JAPAN: Bandai says to postpone sales of new "tamagotchi".
newsitem.headline: Bandai says to postpone sales of new "tamagotchi".

text.p: Japanese toymaker Bandai Co Ltd said on Wednesday it would postpone by a couple of months the debut of new types of "virtual pet" toys featuring an electronic bird.

The firm said the launch of three new models of "tamagotchi", originally due by the end of June, would be delayed to between July and September to make time for it to boost production of existing models to meet soaring demand.

Shipments of "tamagotchi", a chicken-like figure on a liquid crystal display that is fed and cleaned by pressing buttons, have reached about five million units since its debut in November, the company said in a statement.
Sales are forecast to top ten million units by the end of June, as the company plans to supply two million units in May and three million units in June, it said.
Bandai has been hard-pressed to keep up with demand for what has become Japan's hottest toy of 1997.
Shortages have led to the game changing hands at street prices of more than 20 times its retail price of 1,980 yen ($15).
In July, the toymaker will also sell an English version of the virtual pet in Japan, which was recently put on sales in the United States.
The retail price will be the same as the Japanese version.
Tamagotchi starts life as a bird-like image on the screen of an egg-shaped key-ring device. It develops from a chick to a fully grown adult in around 10 days.
However, the owner must feed, groom and soothe the digital creature or else see it waste away and die from neglect.

Bandai, also known for its Dragon Ball and Power Ranger character toys, plans to merge later this year with Sega Enterprises Ltd, maker of the Sega Saturn 32-bit video game player, to create a powerful entertainment entity. ($=125 yen)
